author: Aritra Dutta

contents.content: Bengaluru is like two different cities in one. It's famous for its big tech companies, but it also has peaceful gardens and old buildings to explore. Let’s dive into the best things to do during your 24-hour Bengaluru adventure.

Cubbon Park is a large park in Bangalore. It's 300 acres big, which is a lot of space. If you like parks and trees, this is a good place to visit in Bangalore.
Timings: 6:00 am to 6:00 pm; closed on Mondays and second Tuesdays
Entry Fee: Free

Bangalore has a very grand building called Vidhana Soudha. It's one of the most impressive sights in the city. This building is special because it's where the Karnataka state government works. Inside its nearly 300 rooms, you'll find around 22 different government departments. Built in 1956, Vidhana Soudha is quite tall, reaching almost 46 meters high. It's designed in a beautiful style called Dravidian architecture, which makes it even more special.
Timings: 10:00 AM - 5:30 PM (Closed on weekends and public holidays).
Entry Fee: No entry without permission.

Bangalore has an old palace called Bangalore Palace. It was built way back in the 1800s. The land its on belonged to Reverend John Garrett, the inaugural principal of what is now known as Central College, formerly Central High School. It is owned by Maharaja Biswajit and Maharani Piyali, and one can visit Bangalore Palace to see for yourself how grand Bangalore's history is.
Timings: 10:00 AM - 5:30 PM
Entry Fee : Indian: INR 230, Foreigner: INR 460

Bangalore has another impressive building: Tipu Sultan's Summer Palace. It's inside the old Bangalore Fort. Tipu Sultan, a famous king, used it as his summer home. People called it happy names like "Abode of Happiness.". The palace is old and beautiful, with decorated walls, big arches, and pretty balconies.
Timings: Monday - Saturday: 10:00 AM - 6:00 PM
Sunday: 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM
Entry Fee: Indians- INR 15
Foreigners: INR 200.

Bangalore has a huge garden called Lalbagh. It's famous for plants from all over the world, with almost 2,000 different ones. The garden is very old, started in the 1700s. It's a great place to visit if you love nature and want to see cool plants. You might even see a giant rock that's super old, millions of years old.
Timings: 6:00 AM - 7:00 PM
Entry Fee : Adults: INR 25 (After 8:00 AM)
Children below 12 years old: Free
Camera: INR 60

Conclusion

Bangalore is a fun mix of new and old. Even in one day, you can see lots of things. There are big, green parks like Cubbon Park and Lalbagh Garden. You can also see interesting old buildings, like the big government building and Tipu Sultan's old palace. Bangalore has some interesting things for everyone to explore in one day.

FAQs

Q. How can I spend 1 day in Bangalore?
A. For a perfect 24-hour itinerary, follow our recommendations above. Customize your experience based on your interests.
Q. How many days do I need to visit Bangalore?
A. While one day gives you a glimpse, consider staying longer to explore more facets of this dynamic city.
